{"id":"persona-5s4b.72","title":"KEEP: the signing key is ephemeral with no persistence API at all","description":"persona-core/src/signer.rs:53-78 — SvidSigner generates a fresh ECDSA P-256 keypair in new() and exposes exactly two ways out: public_key_der() and the signing methods. There is no load-from-file, no save, no key path, no rotation schedule, no 'reuse if exists' branch. personad/src/main.rs:31-32 calls SvidSigner::new() once at startup with the comment 'Ephemeral CA keypair — never persisted'.

Why this is worth defending: this is a constraint that deletes an entire category of work rather than a mechanism that manages it. Because the key cannot outlive the process, there is no key file to permission wrongly, no on-disk private key to encrypt or zeroize at rest, no rotation policy to schedule, no 'which key signed this' versioning, no stale-key recovery path, and no migration story between key formats. Restart is the rotation mechanism. The absence of a `load()` constructor is doing more security work than any amount of careful key-file handling would.

The likely 'improvement' to resist: someone hits the consequence — a restarted daemon cannot validate SVIDs it issued before the restart (visible at persona-grpc/src/service.rs:220) — and proposes persisting the key to make validation survive restarts. That trades the whole property away to fix a symptom. The right fix for that symptom is populating the trust bundle store with historical public keys, or accepting that short-lived tokens (5 min TTL, signer.rs:105) simply expire across a restart.

If persistence is ever genuinely required, it should be a deliberate, separately-reviewed change with the threat model written down — not an incremental convenience added to SvidSigner::new().","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:35.626039401Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:35.626039401Z","labels":["review","whats-good"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.72","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:59:35.648316252Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

KEEP note, not a defect. Verified 2026-09-15 that the design it praises is intact: hire-core/src/signer.rs exposes only 'pub fn new() -> Result<Self, SignerError>', which generates a fresh ephemeral key; the sole other constructor, from_pkcs8_der, is #[cfg(test)] and private. There is still no persistence API, so an ephemeral-by-construction signing key cannot be accidentally written to disk. Strengthened since filing: the PKCS#8 DER is no longer retained at all -- the EncodingKey is built once at construction and every copy of the private key in the stack now zeroizes on drop (persona-5s4b.39, commit eb3eddd). Closing as recorded.
